correctness.rationale: The exact frozen entropy-production formula is verified from the forward and reverse currents. Dividing squared lag gives a continuous log-odds secant quotient with derivative numerator \(h(x)-h(q)-(x-q)h'(x)\). For \(0<q<1/2\), it rises past equilibrium to a unique turning point \(x>1/2\), then falls; reflection covers \(q>1/2\), and \(h'(x)\ge4\) proves the balanced case. In the rare-output regime the reciprocal optimizer distance \(y=(1-x_q)^{-1}\) obeys a strictly increasing root equation and is bracketed by \(L+\log L\pm\delta\) for arbitrary fixed \(\delta>0\). Every rate and probability case is proved analytically; the included verifier passed 96,157 supplementary deterministic checks that are not treated as infinite-domain proof.

value.rationale: The optimal global lag-to-entropy-production ratio is a natural thermodynamic performance constant for a binary output network. Unlike the small-lag correlation-time coefficient, it is sharp at a non-equilibrium probability for every asymmetric equilibrium. Its unique optimizer and logarithmically corrected rare-output law establish how large finite-amplitude error can be at a given dissipation scale, supplying a motivated structural extension rather than an arbitrary isolated numerical special case.
